notes: Frame times are reported, not asserted: they are one machine's ops/sec and exist so a human can see whether a change moved the curve. Heap and bundle numbers ARE asserted, by alloc.test.ts and bundle-size.test.ts.

hello-cube.note: Four runs measured -186960, 60688, 60744 and 104088 bytes after a 600-step warm-up. The ceiling is 2.5x the largest.

thousand-entities.note: Three runs measured exactly 9072 bytes. 2x headroom would be 18144; the ceiling is 64 KiB because heapUsed is a whole-process number that a different V8 build can shift, and 64 KiB is still 16x under the 1 MB the standards imply and three orders of magnitude under one small object per entity per frame.

examples/hello-cube.note: gzipBytes is the entry chunk, which is what a first load actually fetches; totalGzipBytes sums all 294 emitted chunks, almost all of them dynamically imported Lite features this scene never reaches. The ceiling is the measurement x 1.1. The plan's Phase 2 target of 250 KB gzipped is NOT met: the entry chunk is 270551 bytes, 20551 over.

templates/2d-topdown.note: Re-measured 2026-09-06 after Phase 8 added @ignifx/ui to the template (a LoadingScreen, a pause Dialog and the two touch widgets, replacing the hand-written src/touch-controls.ts): the entry chunk grew from 1133892 to 1177376 bytes, +43484, which is the whole of @ignifx/ui plus the widget code the template no longer carries itself. The ceiling is the new measurement x 1.1. 797097 of those bytes are @dimforge/rapier2d-compat's dist/rapier.mjs, which inlines its WebAssembly as base64 and is statically imported by @ignifx/physics-2d; the non-Rapier remainder is about 380 KB. The Phase 2 target of 250 KB gzipped does not apply to a template that ships a physics engine.

templates/2d-sidescroller.note: Re-measured the same way, on the same machine, on 2026-09-06. Within 634 bytes of the top-down template: the two carry the same packages and differ only in their own source.

templates/3d-third-person.note: Measured 2026-09-06 on macOS 25.5 arm64 with Node 25.2.1 and Vite 8.2.2; the ceiling is the measurement x 1.1. The entry chunk is a third of a 2D template's because Havok's WebAssembly is NOT inlined: @ignifx/physics declares HavokPhysics.wasm in ignifx.assets.public and @ignifx/vite-plugin copies it into dist/assets/ unhashed (1.4 MB raw, not JavaScript, so it is in neither number here), where Rapier's rapier2d-compat inlines 797 KB of base64 straight into the 2D templates' entry. The second cost of a 3D template is Recast: recast-navigation-*.js gzips to 452964 bytes and inlines its own wasm as a data: URL, but it is a separate chunk that Babylon Lite import()s only when a NavMeshSurface bakes, so it is in totalGzipBytes and not in the first-load entry.

templates/3d-first-person.note: Measured the same way, on the same machine, on 2026-09-06. Within 277 bytes of the third-person template. It carries the Recast chunk too even though it never bakes a navmesh: @ignifx/3d registers its NavigationService unconditionally, so Lite's navigation module is reachable and the chunk is emitted -- it is simply never fetched at runtime, which is what keeps it out of the entry number.

twoD.machine: macOS 25.5 arm64 (Apple Silicon), Node 24.20.0, Vitest 5.0.0, @babylonjs/lite 1.27.0, Chromium (Playwright) + SwiftShader
twoD.note: S6.1. CPU milliseconds per frame with the render loop stopped (app.step), so no presented frame and no SwiftShader rasterisation is in the sample. `loaded` dirties all 1000 movers each frame; `idle` moves nothing. Reported, not asserted, except that `loadedMedianMs` must stay under the 2 ms coding-standards §7 budget and `syncedWhileIdle` must be 0. Chromium quantises performance.now() to 0.1 ms, so the browser medians are coarse.

browser.note: The camera sees 1024 of the 10000 tiles, so chunk culling is exercised.

node.note: A headless app has no surface, so there is no visible rectangle to cull against and every tile is a live sprite. This is the harder of the two measurements.

pixelPerfect.note: S6.3. Blended pixels in a full-canvas readback of a 16x16 one-pixel checkerboard: 0 means every pixel is pure magenta or pure black.
pixelPerfect.counterExampleNote: Linear-sampled atlas at zoom 6.0377 with pixelPerfect off: the whole 64x64 canvas blends.

devtools.note: Phase 10's zero-cost-when-closed exit criterion. The 1,002-entity headless scene is built four times -- plain, devtools, devtools, plain, one app alive at a time -- warmed for 120 frames and then stepped 600 times per block, and each variant's median is taken over its 1,200 samples. Five consecutive runs on 2026-09-06 measured differences of 0.0000, 0.0006, -0.0001, 0.0005 and 0.0036 ms; the row below is the fourth. An earlier two-app design is recorded in the test's header for the record: it read +0.007/+0.000/+0.016 ms with the plain app built first and -0.007/-0.004/-0.008 ms with the devtools app built first, which is construction order rather than devtools, and is why the measurement runs one app at a time.
